name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,698

clue.text: Admired decoration in this clue on prize-winner

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: the winner of a contest is the victor
this clue is 1 across, and the numeral 1 is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone admires a medal pinned on the winner of a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: 'this clue' means its own grid position, with the numeral 1 written as the letter I. 'In' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military award for gallantry, a medal held in great esteem.

clue.text: See 19
Problem for athletes affected covering run

indicators.note: a covering goes over and around something, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: camp means theatrically affected or mannered
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Some athletes suffer a problem when hurt while out on a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like it describes the athletes, but it is the word that supplies CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a painful involuntary muscle spasm, a common complaint among runners and other sportspeople.

clue.text: Men box with hawk-headed god in ensemble

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a chest is a large box
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: Soldiers spar alongside an Egyptian deity as part of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' reads as a verb for fighting but is the noun chest; OR (other ranks) is a crossword standby for men.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians performing together, a typical musical ensemble.

clue.text: Entrance French painter signalling at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only the start of the word is kept

blocks.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter
the opening letter of signalling

explanation.surface: A French artist makes a grand entrance, signalling to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' could be the verb meaning to enchant; here it is the noun for a way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for the act or place of going in, the opposite of egress.

clue.text: 100 at church finding hidden problem

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A hundred people at a church service uncover something concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' is only a link here; 'hidden problem' is the definition, not an instruction to look for a concealed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a concealed drawback or snag in an offer that seems too good to be true.

clue.text: Therapist exercised toes turning hot tap round

indicators.note: something exercised is worked and moved about, so these letters get rearranged
turning something makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A physio works someone's toes, then tests the hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is not part of the turning instruction; it supplies the letter O, which goes in with H and TAP before the three are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles, so is a kind of physical therapist.

clue.text: Small figure coming to point in Scottish palace

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cone is a solid figure that tapers to a point

explanation.surface: A tiny statue is brought to a key spot inside a royal residence in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Scone Palace in Perthshire is where Scottish kings were once crowned; it is not the teatime bake.
explanation.definitionFit: Scone Palace near Perth is a historic Scottish stately home, linked to the coronation Stone of Scone.

clue.text: A mischievous creature sent back, one bringing irritation?

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite order

blocks.note: taken as written
an elf is a small mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A naughty sprite is returned home because it keeps causing annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a description rather than a synonym: a flea irritates the skin it bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas are parasitic insects whose bites make skin itch, so one literally brings irritation to its host.

clue.text: Thought blunder on field should be represented in legal document

indicators.note: to be represented in something is to appear within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: OG is an own goal, a footballer's blunder on the pitch
a citation is a summons to appear in court

explanation.surface: A thoughtless mistake on the sports field ends up recorded in legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: OG for own goal is common in football reports; 'on field' is what points to a sporting blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cogitation is careful deliberate pondering, a formal noun for the process of thinking.

clue.text: Start to eat pastry having at some previous point worn swimsuit?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
clothes that are worn wrap around the wearer, so these letters go round the others

blocks.note: the opening letter of eat
a pie is a pastry dish
once means at some time in the past

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into a pie having earlier been in their swimming costume.
explanation.walkthrough: E and PIE wear ONCE around them. The question mark admits that the hyphenated word, though it can describe other garments, here stands for a swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece is a swimming costume made as a single garment, as opposed to a bikini.

clue.text: What kestrels will do to keep egg clean?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: kestrels famously hang still in the air while hunting
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A naturalist wonders what the birds will do to keep their egg tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the brand name has become a verb for vacuuming. A kestrel is a small falcon known for hovering.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoover is to vacuum a carpet, the brand name serving in British English as a general verb for cleaning.

clue.text: Power in Britain, as corrupt, supported by Con and Lab?

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and altered, so these letters are rearranged
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynic grumbles that power in Britain is as corrupt as the main parties backing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Con and Lab are short for Conservative and Labour, Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisan describes a policy backed by both of two opposing parties, as when Conservatives and Labour agree.

clue.text: Two characters in elevated correspondence?

blocks.note: surface reading: two people exchanging lofty, high-minded letters
setter's reading: a lightweight sheet of mail sent by plane, whose name is two words for a tune and an alphabet character

explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people, but it means letters of the alphabet; 'elevated' points to post carried high in the sky rather than to refined prose.
explanation.definitionFit: An air letter, or aerogramme, is a single folding sheet of paper sent abroad by airmail at a cheap rate.

clue.text: Iron structure in sunset horribly hot inside

indicators.note: something done horribly is badly mangled, so these letters are jumbled
whatever goes inside sits within the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A metal shed gets unbearably hot inside as the sun goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated shelter of curved corrugated iron, used widely by the military in both world wars.

clue.text: Bankers from Poughkeepsie, in their chopper, coming to peak

indicators.note: banks are the edges of a river, so bankers here are the outermost letters
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Americans spell the chopping tool without a final E
the first and last letters of the New York town

explanation.surface: Financiers from a New York town fly by helicopter to a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to Poughkeepsie, a town in New York State, so the chopper is spelt the American way. 'Chopper' also suggests a helicopter, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or tip of something, such as the summit of a mountain.

clue.text: In film, lost climbing team should make admission

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about a stranded alien
lorn is a poetic word for forlorn or lost
a team is a side of men

explanation.surface: In a movie, a mountaineering party gone astray must make a confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission' suggests confessing, which the surface leans on; here it means being let in, as to a course or club.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of officially joining an institution, the same as being granted entry to it.

clue.text: Loud organ causes apprehension

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A booming church organ makes listeners uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' calls up the musical instrument, especially next to 'Loud', but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension is anxious dread about what may happen, a close synonym for the emotion of being afraid.

clue.text: The PM arose to change prevailing mood

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister stood up to shift the national mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as politics, but every letter of the first three words is simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place or occasion is its general feeling or tone, the mood that hangs over it.

clue.text: Show tune's in tune: fly out with Navy men

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical number about sailors taking off, delivered perfectly on pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In tune' looks like a description of the singing, but its letters join the jumble with fly and Navy men.
explanation.definitionFit: This Rodgers and Hart number comes from the 1937 Broadway musical Babes in Arms and became a jazz standard.

clue.text: Forest with walnut ultimately burning

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire, the setting of As You Like It
the closing letter of walnut

explanation.surface: Woodland full of nut trees is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is a real Warwickshire woodland and the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent comes from the Latin for burning and describes passionate, fervent feeling, so burning works in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Trace local banished from Ireland for example

indicators.note: what is banished is sent away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: the local is a British word for one's neighbourhood pub
the Republic of Ireland is one example of a republic

explanation.surface: Someone tries to find a pub regular who was sent out of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' could be a verb meaning to track down, as the surface suggests; it is the noun, a surviving remnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a surviving remnant of something from the past, so it is a trace left behind.

clue.text: Legally land small turtle, leaving trap

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
to pin is to trap or hold fast

explanation.surface: Someone lawfully lands a little turtle after it escapes a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legally' signals the Latin word used in legal language; 'land' looks like a verb about catching the turtle, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for earth or ground and appears in legal terms such as terra firma and terra nullius.

clue.text: Emancipate wife? Detrimental to give independence!

blocks.note: to emancipate is to set free
W is the abbreviation for wife
ill can mean harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether liberating a wife would harm her by granting autonomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation break the clue into an argument, but it is a plain charade; W for wife is a crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the power to act by one's own choice, a form of personal self-determination.

clue.text: Hunted creature's mournful cry heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a wail is a long sorrowful cry

explanation.surface: The sad call of a hunted animal can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the cry belong to the creature; in fact the two are linked only by sounding alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales have long been hunted for oil and meat, so the description fits the sea mammal.

clue.text: Pose holding large fish, crossing river to find narrow shelter

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it, so one piece goes around another
to cross something is to span it, so one piece straddles another

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to pose
L is the abbreviation for large
a tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone poses with a big fish while wading across a river, looking for somewhere to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate containers sit side by side, each built before they are joined; the tench is a European freshwater fish of ponds and slow rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A slit trench is a narrow trench dug by soldiers for cover against blast and gunfire.

clue.text: Poet eschewing university calls for port

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid or give up, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A writer who skipped college demands to go to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the fortified wine a poet might call for; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a major seaport in Yemen at the entrance to the Red Sea.

clue.text: Ace times in Arts Centre rocking in fashionable way?

indicators.note: something rocking is shaken about, so these letters are rearranged
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
in multiplication, six times four is six by four
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A great evening at the arts venue swinging in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' means a road, not a manner; Carnaby Street in London's Soho was the heart of 1960s Swinging London fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnaby Street is a London shopping street famed for trendy clothing boutiques, so it is literally a stylish road.
